title: Cube Cash Tycoon
pitch: Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!
core_loop: Each player gets a bright plot with a dropper that spawns a 1-cash cube every 2 seconds onto a conveyor. The conveyor carries cubes to a collector at the end, and the server adds each cube's value to the player's Cash leaderstat and destroys the cube. Two buy pads sit off to the side of the walking area: a second dropper for 25 cash and a faster conveyor for 50 cash. Touching a pad with enough cash buys the upgrade once, so income climbs and the numbers go up.

modules.purpose: PREBUILT (do not rewrite): palette, sound ids, play(name, parent?), burst(at, color?, count?), shake(intensity?, seconds?) client-only, styleLighting() server, part(props) -> Part.

Shared constants. Returns a table with: DROP_INTERVAL=2, CUBE_VALUE=1, CUBE_SIZE=Vector3.new(1.5,1.5,1.5), CONVEYOR_SPEED=8, FAST_CONVEYOR_SPEED=16, DROPPER_COST=25, CONVEYOR_COST=50, PLOT_SIZE=Vector3.new(40,1,40), PLOT_SPACING=60, MAX_PLOTS=8, CONVEYOR_LENGTH=24, MAX_CUBES_PER_PLOT=30, colors (PLOT_COLOR, CONVEYOR_COLOR, CUBE_COLOR, DROPPER_COLOR, COLLECTOR_COLOR, BUTTON_COLOR, BOUGHT_COLOR), REMOTES_FOLDER='TycoonRemotes', and REMOTE_NOTIFY='Notify' (server to client message string).

Builds the world from parts at runtime (baseplate, one plot per slot index) with a small part count (about 15 per plot, 8 plots max). Returns {buildBase(): Part, buildPlot(index:number): Plot} where Plot = {origin:CFrame, spawnCFrame:CFrame, conveyor:Part, conveyorDir:Vector3, droppers:{Part} (first one active, second one hidden or greyed until bought), dropperSlot2:Part, collector:Part, dropperButton:Part, conveyorButton:Part}. Buttons sit on the side of the plot, at least 6 studs from the spawn and the conveyor path, so walking never triggers them accidentally. Uses Anchored parts, with no coplanar surfaces. The conveyor is a long thin part whose top surface cubes ride on.

Server-side tycoon logic. Returns {new(player:Player, plot:Plot): Tycoon, Tycoon:destroy()}. On new: starts a drop loop that spawns an unanchored-or-velocity-driven Cube (value Config.CUBE_VALUE, stored as a NumberValue or attribute) from each active dropper every DROP_INTERVAL, with the first cube spawned immediately. Cubes move along the conveyor using AssemblyLinearVelocity or a Heartbeat step at the current conveyor speed, with a cap of MAX_CUBES_PER_PLOT. The collector's Touched event adds the cube value to player.leaderstats.Cash and destroys the cube, counting 'cubes_collected'. Wires the button Touched events, each debounced and only once per player: dropperButton costs DROPPER_COST and activates the second dropper (counts 'dropper_bought'); conveyorButton costs CONVEYOR_COST and sets the conveyor speed to FAST_CONVEYOR_SPEED (counts 'conveyor_bought'). The server checks Cash >= cost, deducts it, recolors the button to BOUGHT_COLOR, and fires Notify to the client. Counts 'cubes_dropped' per spawn.

Entry point. Creates the remotes folder and the Notify RemoteEvent in ReplicatedStorage. Calls PlotBuilder.buildBase() and counts 'map_built'. On PlayerAdded (and for players already in game) creates the leaderstats folder with Cash=0, assigns the next free plot index, builds the plot, creates a Tycoon, and teleports the character to plot.spawnCFrame on CharacterAdded (counts 'plot_assigned'). On PlayerRemoving it destroys the Tycoon, removes the plot, and frees the slot. Also creates a SpawnLocation if needed so respawning works.

Creates a ScreenGui at runtime showing a big 'Cash: N' label that reads player.leaderstats.Cash (waiting with a timeout), a small hint line 'Touch the green pads to buy: Dropper 25 / Fast Belt 50', and a short toast when the Notify remote fires. Waits for the remotes via WaitForChild with a timeout. UI only, with no gameplay authority.

Feature: Themed plots and plot claiming for multiplayer: build a bright central spawn plaza (stone tiles, a fountain, lamp posts, trees) with 6 plots arranged in a ring around it. Each plot has its own theme with distinct floor material, colors and 3-5 decoration props built from parts: Candy (pink/mint, lollipops), Lava (basalt + glowing neon cracks), Ice (glacier/ice, crystals), Jungle (grass, palm trees), Neon City (dark slate floor, neon strips), Desert (sand, cacti). No grey or default-colored parts anywhere: the conveyor rails, dropper bodies and pads take the plot's theme colors. Players spawn in the plaza and walk onto a glowing CLAIM gate at the front of an empty plot (BillboardGui 'Claim <Theme> Plot') to claim it; the plot then shows a sign with the owner's name, starts the dropper, and only the owner can use its pads. One plot per player; a player's plot is freed when they leave. If a player has not claimed within 20 seconds, auto-claim the nearest free plot for them so the loop always starts. -- Shared config ModuleScript returning a table. It holds CLAIM_TIMEOUT=20, the ring layout (plaza center, plaza radius, ring radius, plot size) and an ordered list of 6 themes: Candy, Lava, Ice, Jungle, Neon City and Desert. Each theme has a name, floor Material and Color3, an accent color, rail color, dropper body color, pad colors, a glow color, and a decor list of 3-5 prop descriptors. Props are lollipops, neon-crack strips, crystals, palm trees, neon strips or cacti, each with a kind, offset and color. Every color is explicit and non-grey, and no part may use default materials or colors. Also exposes helper getTheme(index). Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: plaza_built, themes_built, plots_claimed, auto_claims.

Feature: Dropper tiers and an upgrade tree, data-driven: a new ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades config lists about 12 upgrades with id, name, cost, requires (parent id) and effect. Tree: 4 dropper slots (Dropper 2/3/4 each requiring the previous), 3 dropper tiers that change the ore every dropper spits out (Bronze ore 1 cash -> Silver 3 -> Gold 8 -> Diamond 20; each tier has its own color and material, e.g. Gold is shiny Foil yellow, Diamond is glass cyan with sparkles), 2 conveyor speed upgrades, and 2 'Cash Multiplier' upgrades (x1.5, x2) on the collector. Costs grow so a full tree takes about 8-10 minutes (first buy costs 10 and is affordable within 10 seconds). An UpgradeService on the server owns which upgrades each player has bought, validates requires + cost atomically, applies the effect to that player's Tycoon, and fires an UpgradeBought remote to the client. Buy pads on the owner's plot show a BillboardGui price tag with the upgrade name and cost, are only visible once their parent is bought, turn the plot's accent color when affordable, and vanish after purchase. Bump counters upgrades_bought and tier_upgrades. -- Pure data ModuleScript with no requires and no side effects. Returns {list = {...}, byId = {...}, ores = {...}}. Each upgrade has id, name, cost, requires (parent id or nil) and effect. Effect shapes: {kind='dropper', slots=n}, {kind='tier', tier=n}, {kind='speed', mult=x}, {kind='cashMult', mult=x}. The 10 upgrades (id, cost, requires): dropper2 10 none; tier_silver 30 dropper2; speed1 60 dropper2; dropper3 100 dropper2; mult1 (x1.5) 200 tier_silver; tier_gold 350 tier_silver; speed2 500 speed1; dropper4 800 dropper3; mult2 (x2) 1500 mult1; tier_diamond 2500 tier_gold. A comment block holds the budget math (a full tree takes about 8-10 minutes). `ores` is indexed by tier: 1 Bronze (value 1, orange-copper, Metal), 2 Silver (3, light grey, Metal), 3 Gold (8, yellow, Foil), 4 Diamond (20, cyan, Glass, sparkles=true). Each ore has name, value, color, material and sparkles. byId is built at load time. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: upgrades_bought, tier_upgrades.

It owns per-player state {owned = {[id]=true}, pads = {...}}. init() creates the RemoteEvent 'UpgradeBought' in ReplicatedStorage; this is the only place it is created. onPlotClaimed builds one buy pad per upgrade on the owner's plot, using the exact plot fields PlotBuilder returns (read them from that file; no guessed fallbacks). After that it recomputes the modifiers (slots = 1 + dropper upgrades, ore = highest tier owned (default 1), speedMult = product of owned speed mults, cashMult = highest owned cashMult (default 1)) and calls Tycoon.setModifiers(player, mods). It then calls UpgradeBought:FireClient(player, id, mods). It bumps ForgeTelemetry.count('upgrades_bought', 1) on every purchase and ForgeTelemetry.count('tier_upgrades', 1) when effect.kind == 'tier'; these counters are bumped only here. onPlayerRemoving destroys the pads, disconnects connections and clears the state. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: upgrades_bought, tier_upgrades.

Feature: Rebirth with a multiplier: once a player has bought every upgrade in the tree OR has at least 5000 cash, a glowing golden Rebirth altar on their plot (and a Rebirth button in the HUD) lets them rebirth. A RebirthService on the server validates the requirement (cost 5000 cash, doubling each rebirth), resets their Cash to 0 and their bought upgrades to none (rebuilding the plot's buy pads via UpgradeService), increments a Rebirths leaderstat, and gives a permanent cash multiplier of 1 + 0.5 * rebirths applied to every collected ore. The client shows a full-screen golden flash and 'REBIRTH x<mult>!' banner. Bump counters rebirths and rebirth_denied. -- Shared tunables table: baseCost=5000, costGrowth=2, multPerRebirth=0.5, requestCooldown (seconds), altar color/size, flash duration, banner duration. Also pure helper functions costFor(rebirths) = baseCost * costGrowth^rebirths and multiplierFor(rebirths) = 1 + multPerRebirth * rebirths, used by both server and client so the HUD button label matches the server. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: rebirths, rebirth_denied.

The client shows a full-screen golden flash and 'REBIRTH x<mult>!' banner. Bump counters rebirths and rebirth_denied. -- Server-authoritative rebirth system, a ModuleScript required and initialised from Game.server. It creates the RemoteEvents in one place under ReplicatedStorage (RebirthRequest client->server, RebirthResult server->client carrying ok, new multiplier, next cost and a reason). Per player it keeps a rebirth count and creates an integer 'Rebirths' leaderstat in the existing leaderstats folder (wait for it with a timeout). It sets the player attribute 'RebirthMult' to multiplierFor(rebirths), which Tycoon reads, so there is no circular require. Exposes init(), onPlotClaimed(player, plot) and onPlotReleased(player), and tryRebirth(player). onPlotClaimed builds a glowing golden Neon altar part from code on the claimed plot, using the plot data fields that PlotBuilder and PlotClaimService already return and placed off the spawn and walking path. The altar has a billboard showing the cost and a ProximityPrompt that calls tryRebirth. onPlotReleased destroys the altar. tryRebirth applies a per-player cooldown and checks, in one step, eligible = UpgradeService.hasAll(player) or Cash >= cost. If not eligible it fires RebirthResult with ok=false and counts 'rebirth_denied'. If eligible it sets Cash to 0, calls UpgradeService.resetPlayer(player) to clear purchases and rebuild the pads, increments the rebirth count and the Rebirths leaderstat, updates the RebirthMult attribute and the altar billboard, fires RebirthResult with ok=true, and counts 'rebirths'. The RebirthRequest handler only calls tryRebirth and trusts nothing from the client. Players already in the game at startup are handled by looping Players:GetPlayers() and also connecting PlayerAdded. Bumps counters rebirths and rebirth_denied, each in this module only. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: rebirths, rebirth_denied.

Feature: Satisfying cash-in feedback: when ore reaches the owner's collector, the server fires a CashIn remote to that owner with the amount, the ore tier and the collector position. A client CashInFx script then plays a short coin 'cha-ching' sound (pitch rises slightly with tier; use sound ids that load in Studio, e.g. rbxasset://sounds/electronicpingshort.wav), bursts a ParticleEmitter of gold sparkles at the collector, floats a '+$N' BillboardGui text that rises and fades (colored by tier), and pulses the HUD cash label. Purchases play an upgrade 'pop' sound with a confetti burst; throttle effects so at most 6 popups per second. The collector itself gets a glowing PointLight and a slowly spinning neon ring. Bump counter cashin_fx_sent. -- Pure shared tunables for cash-in feedback, returned as one table. Fields: RING_TAG = 'CashInRing'; MAX_POPUPS_PER_SECOND = 6; CASHIN_SOUND_ID = 'rbxasset://sounds/electronicpingshort.wav'; POP_SOUND_ID (a Studio-loadable rbxasset sound, e.g. rbxasset://sounds/button.wav); BASE_PITCH = 1 and PITCH_PER_TIER = 0.06 (capped); TIER_COLORS, an array of Color3 indexed by tier with a helper function colorForTier(tier) that clamps the index to the array; RING_SPIN_DEG_PER_SEC = 45; light Brightness/Range/Color; and the remote names 'CashIn' and 'PurchaseFx'. No requires. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: cashin_fx_sent, purchase_fx_sent.

Feature: Shop UI built with the UI kit (the house Theme, rounded panels, big readable buttons): a 'SHOP' button on the left edge of the HUD opens a panel listing every upgrade from ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades as cards (color swatch, name, effect text, cost, and state: Owned / Locked (needs X) / Buy). Pressing Buy sends a BuyUpgrade RemoteEvent; the server (UpgradeService) validates plot ownership, requires and cost exactly like a pad touch, then replies with the updated owned list so cards refresh. Cards the player cannot afford are dimmed; the panel closes with an X button or the same SHOP button. Must fit a phone-width screen. Bump counters shop_opened and shop_purchases. -- Pure shared UI kit for the house Theme. Returns one table with panel, card, text, accent, good, dim and locked colors, the font, corner radius, stroke, min button height (at least 44px) and padding. It also has small helpers: UiTheme.roundify(guiObject, radius) adds a UICorner, and UiTheme.makeButton(props) returns a big readable TextButton. Colors are taken from the existing HUD and cash palette (check Hud.client.luau and CashInConfig) so the look matches. It has no side effects and no server code. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: shop_opened, shop_purchases.

Bump counters shop_opened and shop_purchases. -- Client-only shop UI in its own ScreenGui (ResetOnSpawn=false). It builds a 'SHOP' button on the left edge of the screen, vertically centered and clear of the Cash HUD, that toggles a rounded panel with a title, an X close button and a ScrollingFrame list. The panel uses scale sizing with a UISizeConstraint (max about 420x520) so it fits a phone-width screen, and the text is large and readable. It requires ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades and iterates every upgrade, using that module's exact existing field names for id, name, cost, requires and effect. If there is no effect-text field, it builds the effect text from the data fields that exist. Each card shows a color swatch, name, effect text, cost, and a state button. Owned shows a disabled 'Owned' label. Locked shows 'Locked (needs <name of required upgrade>)' when a required id is not owned. Otherwise it shows a 'Buy' button. Cards where cost exceeds the Cash leaderstat are dimmed (transparency and darker text), and this refreshes on leaderstats Cash.Changed. It WaitForChilds the remotes ReplicatedStorage/BuyUpgrade and ReplicatedStorage/ShopSync with a timeout and fails soft if they are missing. Opening the panel does ShopSync:FireServer() to request the owned list. It listens to ShopSync.OnClientEvent(ownedIds) (an array of upgrade ids) and re-renders the cards. Feature: Data saving: a DataService on the server saves each player's Cash, TotalEarned, Rebirths and owned upgrade ids with DataStoreService (store 'CubeCashTycoon_v1', key 'p_<UserId>'), loading on join before their Tycoon starts (re-applying owned upgrades), autosaving every 60 seconds, on PlayerRemoving and in game:BindToClose. Every DataStore call is wrapped in pcall with a couple of retries; when DataStore is unavailable (Studio without API access, or any error) it falls back to an in-memory table so the game still runs with no errors or warnings in the output (one quiet print, never warn). Bump counters data_loaded and data_saved. -- ModuleScript owning all persistence. It returns a table with these functions. DataService.init() runs once: it creates the store, starts the 60s autosave loop (task.spawn with task.wait(60), saving every loaded player), connects Players.PlayerRemoving (save, then drop the cache) and sets game:BindToClose to save all loaded players. It does not require Tycoon or the claim logic. DataService.loadPlayer(player) yields. It reads key 'p_'..UserId through a retrying pcall wrapper and falls back to the in-memory table on failure. It normalises the result to {Cash=0, TotalEarned=0, Rebirths=0, Upgrades={}}, caches it per player, and bumps ForgeTelemetry.count('data_loaded',1) exactly once per player. DataService.applyPlayer(player) waits up to about 10s for player.leaderstats, then sets Cash, TotalEarned and Rebirths from the cache. It restores the Rebirths state through RebirthService and the owned ids through UpgradeService.restoreOwned(player, ids). It is safe to call even if loadPlayer failed (defaults). DataService.savePlayer(player) snapshots the current Cash, TotalEarned and Rebirths (from leaderstats or the owning service) plus UpgradeService.getOwnedIds(player). It writes with UpdateAsync or SetAsync inside a pcall with 3 attempts and task.wait(1) between them, and falls back to the memory table. It skips players whose data was never loaded, so a fresh default cannot overwrite a real save. A per-player saving flag prevents duplicate saves from PlayerRemoving plus BindToClose. It bumps ForgeTelemetry.count('data_saved',1) once per successful save, whether to DataStore or to memory. Persistence uses DataStoreService:GetDataStore('CubeCashTycoon_v1'), obtained inside a pcall. If that fails or a call errors, the service sets useMemory=true and prints one quiet message ('DataService: using in-memory store') a single time. It never calls warn or error. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: data_loaded, data_saved.

Bump counters data_loaded and data_saved. -- ModuleScript owning all persistence. It returns a table with these functions. DataService.init() runs once: it creates the store, starts the 60s autosave loop (task.spawn with task.wait(60), saving every loaded player), connects Players.PlayerRemoving (save, then drop the cache) and sets game:BindToClose to save all loaded players. It does not require Tycoon or the claim logic. DataService.loadPlayer(player) yields. It reads key 'p_'..UserId through a retrying pcall wrapper and falls back to the in-memory table on failure. It normalises the result to {Cash=0, TotalEarned=0, Rebirths=0, Upgrades={}}, caches it per player, and bumps ForgeTelemetry.count('data_loaded',1) exactly once per player. DataService.applyPlayer(player) waits up to about 10s for player.leaderstats, then sets Cash, TotalEarned and Rebirths from the cache. It restores the Rebirths state through RebirthService and the owned ids through UpgradeService.restoreOwned(player, ids). It is safe to call even if loadPlayer failed (defaults). DataService.savePlayer(player) snapshots the current Cash, TotalEarned and Rebirths (from leaderstats or the owning service) plus UpgradeService.getOwnedIds(player). It writes with UpdateAsync or SetAsync inside a pcall with 3 attempts and task.wait(1) between them, and falls back to the memory table. Rebirth multiplier: a permanent x1.5, x2.0, x2.5 and so on, shown on the HUD and next to the player's name on the leaderboard.
Cosmetic plot trims: neon lamp colours and a golden collector skin unlock at rebirths 2, 3 and 5.

acceptance: The player is auto-claimed a plot and placed on it within 3 seconds of joining, with plaza_built, themes_built (6) and plots_claimed incrementing.
The free Bronze dropper starts dropping cubes within 5 seconds and the first cube is collected within about 8 seconds, which gives cubes_collected >= 1 and cashin_fx_sent >= 1.
Each collection shows a +$N floating text and the HUD cash ticks up, with an income readout like '+$5/s'.
The first BuyPad (Dropper 2 at $20) is affordable within about 15 s and, once bought, bumps upgrades_bought and purchase_fx_sent.
BuyPads show a green PriceBillboard when affordable and red otherwise, and only the next 1-3 pads are visible.
Stepping on a pad without enough cash plays Error, leaves cash unchanged and does not buy.
The SHOP button opens a Panel (shop_opened) whose buttons buy upgrades server-side (shop_purchases) and mirror the BuyPad costs.
Buying an ore tier bumps tier_upgrades, changes the cube colour and shows a RewardPopup.
Live ore cubes never exceed 60 per plot and cubes do not collide with the player.
The tutorial arrow completes at least 3 steps (tutorial_steps) and disappears afterward.
Rebirth is blocked below $25k, and at or above it resets cash and unlocks, raises the multiplier and Rebirths stat and bumps rebirths.
The TOP TYCOONS board shows the solo player and refreshes (leaderboard_refresh), and data_loaded and data_saved fire for the player.

first_60s.beat: The player spawns on the plaza facing a plot ring of 6 themed plots and a glowing plot sign. The plaza and themes are already built.
The player is auto-claimed the nearest plot and teleported onto it. Saved data loads and the HUD shows $0 and the arrow points at the free Bronze dropper.
The free Bronze dropper starts dropping cubes that roll along the conveyor.
The first cube reaches the collector. The collector flashes, cha-ching plays, +$5 floats up and the HUD ticks. This is the first reward.
The cash-in FX batches fire as cubes keep paying and the HUD shows '+$5/s'. The price tag on the Dropper 2 pad turns green at $20.
The player steps on the glowing Dropper 2 pad (set off the spawn path). The pad pops, the dropper rises and sparkles burst.
The purchase effects and tutorial arrow step advance, now pointing at the SHOP button.
The player opens the SHOP panel, then buys Conveyor Speed 1 for $45 from the grid.
A Silver ore tier is bought, the cubes change colour and a RewardPopup appears. The TOP TYCOONS board refreshes with the player on it.
